title: Molecular Classification of Erythrodermas Based on a Molecular Classifier
summary: In this study, a new diagnostic method is being evaluated to help identify the cause of a severe skin redness affecting more than 90% of the body surface (erythroderma). Existing tissue samples will be analyzed using a specialized molecular test, and the results will be compared with previous diagnoses made by physicians. No additional procedures or treatments will be performed. The aim is to determine whether this method can improve the accuracy and reliability of diagnosis.

interventions.name: This is a non-interventional, diagnostic multicenter study conducted at the study sites Freiburg and Augsburg. The aim is to evaluate the molecular classifier for the precise classification of erythroderma and to investigate the correlation between clinical, histopathological, and molecular paramete

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnosis of erythroderma (clinical involvement of >90% of the body surface area) with suspected psoriasis, eczema, or other differential diagnoses, persisting for >4 weeks
- Skin biopsy performed at the time of diagnosis, with optional follow-up biopsies under targeted therapy (e.g., biologic therapy) for psoriasis/eczema
- Written informed consent for the use of residual tissue material obtained during routine diagnostic procedures
Exclusion criteria:
- Erythroderma <4 weeks in duration or known alternative cause (e.g., drug eruption, contact dermatitis)
- Lack of informed consent
- Insufficient tissue material for molecular classifier analysis
